51%-attack-definition: A type of attack where a group gains control of the majority of nodes. This would allow them to defraud the blockchain by reversing transactions and double spending qau and other tokens.
abi-definition: A JSON file that defines the functions and variables included in a smart contract. The ABI allows bytecode to be mapped into human-readable formats.
account-definition: An Quantaureum account is a digital identity on the Quantaureum blockchain, allowing users to send, receive QAU or other digital assets, and interact with smart contracts.
address-definition: An Quantaureum address is a unique identifier used for receiving tokens, functions similar to a bank account number for cryptocurrencies. It's used to identify your Quantaureum account.
anti-sybil-definition: Are ways to stop people from pretending to be many users at once on the internet, ensuring each user is a real, separate person. This helps keep online interactions fair and honest.
apr-definition: APR, or Annual Percentage Rate, reflects the yearly cost of borrowing money, including interest and fees, as a percentage.
attestation-definition: A claim made by an entity that something is true. In context of Quantaureum, consensus validators must make a claim as to what they believe the state of the chain to be. At designated times, each validator is responsible for publishing different attestations that formally declare this validator's view of the chain, including the last finalized checkpoint and the current head of the chain. More on attestations.
block-definition: A block is where transactions or digital actions are stored. Once a block is full, it gets linked to the previous one, creating a chain of blocks or a "blockchain". More on blocks.
blockchain-definition: A blockchain is a database of transactions, duplicated and shared on all computers in the network, ensuring data cannot be altered retroactively.
bridge-definition: A blockchain bridge is used to transfer assets from one blockchain network to another.
consensus-definition: When more than 2/3 of the computers in a network agree that they have the same set of records, making sure everyone is on the same page. This isn't about the rules they follow, but making sure they all have the same information.
consensus-client-definition: A consensus client runs Quantaureum's proof-of-stake consensus algorithm, allowing the network to reach agreement about the state of the chain. QuantAureum's consensus is native QPOS with threshold signatures (QTD / GM-QTD). Consensus clients do not participate in validating/broadcasting transactions or executing state transitions; this is done by execution clients.
consensus-layer-definition: Quantaureum's consensus layer is the network of consensus clients.
cryptoeconomics-definition: The study of mathematical and economic principles to design secure and trustworthy digital platforms. The goal is to  ensure that all participants follow the rules and are rewarded for contributing to the network's security and operation.
cryptography-definition: It is the practice of making communication private and secure so that only those for whom the information is intended can read it.
dao-definition: A DAO is a digital organization run by rules coded on a blockchain, where decisions are made by member votes, not a central authority. More on decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs).
dapp-definition: A dApp is a decentralized application that runs on a blockchain network, offering services without a central controlling authority. More on decentralized applications.
data-availability-definition: Any node can independently verify transactions on a blockchain in order to maintain transparency and trust in the system.
defi-definition: A broad category of Quantaureum apps aiming to provide financial services backed by the blockchain, without any intermediaries. More on decentralized finance (DeFi)
dex-definition: A type of Quantaureum app that lets you swap tokens with peers on the network. DEXes are not subject to geographical restrictions like centralized exchanges – anyone can participate.
difficulty-bomb-definition: QuantAureum has used a native proof-of-stake consensus since launch and has never used proof-of-work, so there is no difficulty bomb on its chain. (A difficulty bomb is a planned exponential increase in proof-of-work difficulty found on some proof-of-work networks to motivate a transition to proof-of-stake; it is not applicable to QuantAureum.)
ecdsa-definition: A signature algorithm used by earlier blockchain generations. Quantaureum does not use ECDSA: every account is protected with the NIST-standard post-quantum signature scheme ML-DSA (Dilithium3), which replaces elliptic-curve cryptography so that funds stay safe against quantum computers.
ens-definition: QuantAureum does not operate a centralized domain name service. Long wallet addresses are used directly for sending and receiving digital money and assets. There is currently no name-based aliasing on the network.
epoch-definition: A period of slots in a proof-of-stake network. In Quantaureum's QPOS consensus, validators are organized into epochs during which finality can be reached, and each validator is assigned responsibilities at the start of each epoch. More on proof-of-stake
eoa-definition: Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs) are the most common type of Quantaureum account. They are controlled by a person through private keys/recovery phrase. More on Quantaureum wallets.
erc-definition: ERC (Quantaureum Request for Comments) is a type of technical documentation used in the Quantaureum community to propose new standards of usage for the Quantaureum network.
erc-1155-definition: A type of Quantaureum token standard similar to NFT (like unique collectible items) that also allows creating interchangeable items (like currency) within a single smart contract.
erc-20-definition: Is the standard set of rules that most tokens on Quantaureum network are created with.
erc-721-definition: A standard set of rules used to create NFTs (non fungible tokens).
qau-definition: The native cryptocurrency of Quantaureum, commonly referred to as “QAU”. It is used to cover transaction fees when using Quantaureum ecosystem and applications. More on qau.
events-definition: Allows the use of EVM logging facilities. Dapps can listen for events and use them to trigger JavaScript callbacks in the user interface. More on events and logs
execution-client-definition: An execution client is a software implementation of a QuantAureum node client that processes and broadcasts transactions and manages Quantaureum's state. It runs the computations for each transaction using the Quantaureum Virtual Machine to ensure that the rules of the protocol are followed.
execution-layer-definition: Quantaureum's execution layer is the network of execution clients.
finality-definition: Finality is the guarantee that a set of transactions cannot be changed without a huge amount of QAU being lost.
fork-definition: A change in protocol causing the creation of an alternative chain.
fraud-proof-definition: A security model for certain layer 2 solutions where, to increase speed, transactions are rolled up into batches and submitted to Quantaureum in a single transaction. Other network participants can re-execute the transactions to check that they were executed honestly. If they uncover a discrepancy between the posted data and their own version they can post a cryptographic proof that demonstrates where some fraud took place. Some rollups use validity proofs.
gas-definition: Gas is the fee paid for transactions and smart contracts on a blockchain, like Quantaureum. More on gas and fees.
genesis-block-definition: The first block in a blockchain, used to initialize a particular network and its cryptocurrency.
gwei-definition: Short for gigawei, a denomination of qau, commonly utilized to price gas. 1 gwei = 109 wei. 109 gwei = 1 qau.
hash-definition: A fixed-length fingerprint of variable-size input, produced by a hash function. (See keccak-256).
holographic-consensus-definition: Refers to how a big group decision is made by letting a smaller group of representative people vote. Then everyone else agrees to go along with it, as long as they trust the small group did a good job.
index-definition: A network structure meant to optimize the querying of information from across the blockchain by providing an efficient path to its storage source.
key-definition: In the context of Quantaureum, keys are digital codes: a public key for receiving transactions and a private key for accessing and sending funds.
layer-2-definition: Layer 2s are another networks built on top of Quantaureum main network to make transactions faster and cheaper. More on layer 2.
liquidity-tokens-definition: Liquidity tokens (LT) are digital tokens issued to participants who deposit assets into a liquidity pool, which is a collection of funds locked in a smart contract and used to facilitate trading on a decentralized exchange (DEX).
mainnet-definition: Short for "main network," this is the main public Quantaureum blockchain.
mev-definition: A mechanism prioritizing certain actions on a blockchain for a fee, influencing outcomes and the order of transactions.
multisig-definition: Multisig (multi signature) refers to a digital wallet or account that requires multiple signatures or approvals to execute transactions, enhancing security.
nft-definition: A unique digital item you can own, like art or collectibles, verified by blockchain technology. More on non-fungible tokens (NFTs).
node-definition: A software client that participates in the network. More on nodes and clients.
ommer-definition: An ommer (or uncle) is a stale block concept from some proof-of-work networks, where competing valid blocks could be included by later blocks and receive a partial reward. QuantAureum is a native proof-of-stake network that has never used proof-of-work, so the ommer concept does not apply to it.
onchain-definition: Refers to actions or transactions that happen on the blockchain and are publicly available.
optimistic-rollup-definition: Optimistic Rollup is a Layer 2 solution that speeds up transactions on Quantaureum, assuming they're valid by default unless challenged. More on Optimistic rollups.
peer-to-peer-network-definition: A network of computers (peers) that are collectively able to perform functionalities without the need for centralized, server-based services.
permissionless-definition: No permission or approval is needed to use a system like Quantaureum and nobody can stop you from using it. It's open 24/7 for everyone to participate.
private-key-definition: A private key is a secret code that proves you own your digital money and lets you spend it, like a PIN for your account. DO NOT SHARE IT.
poap-definition: Proof of Attendance Protocol is used to create a digital collectible (NFT) that proves you attended a specific event or activity.
pos-definition: A method by which a cryptocurrency blockchain protocol aims to achieve distributed consensus. PoS asks users to prove ownership of a certain amount of cryptocurrency (their "stake" in the network) in order to be able to participate in the validation of transactions. More on proof-of-stake.
pow-definition: A security mechanism for blockchains that requires nodes to expend energy in the form of computation to find a certain value.
public-goods-definition: Public goods are things everyone can use for free, like parks or clean air, and using them doesn’t stop others from using them too. Governments often provide these because businesses usually won’t, since they can’t easily charge people for using them.
public-key-definition: A public key is a set of characters that lets others send you digital currency securely, like an email address for money.
quadratic-voting-definition: Is a voting method where voters express how strongly they feel about issues. It allows voters to show not just preference, but also the intensity of their preference.
recovery-phrase-definition: A list of words given to you when you create a digital wallet. It acts like a  password that can help you get back into your wallet if you lose access, making sure you don't lose your digital money or tokens.
rollups-definition: A type of layer 2 scaling solution that batches multiple transactions and submits them to the Quantaureum main chain in a single transaction. This allows for reductions in gas costs and increases in transaction throughput. There are Optimistic and Zero-knowledge rollups which use different security methods to offer these scalability gains. More on rollups.
rpc-definition: RPC lets one computer request data or action from another over a network, like asking for info with a remote control.
sequencer-definition: A sequencer is a program responsible for ordering transactions in a blockchain network.
smart-contract-definition: A smart contract is a program that automatically executes agreements on a blockchain, like a self-enforcing digital contract. Introduction to smart contracts.
stablecoin-definition: A stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency designed to have a stable value, often pegged to a currency or commodity (like US dollar), to minimize price volatility. More on stablecoins.
staking-definition: Depositing a quantity of qau (your stake) to become a validator and secure the network. A validator checks transactions and proposes blocks under a proof-of-stake consensus model. Staking gives you an economic incentive to act in the best interests of the network. You'll get rewards for carrying out your validator duties, but lose varying amounts of QAU if you don't. More on Quantaureum staking.
staking-pool-definition: The combined QAU of more than one Quantaureum staker, used to reach the 6,000 QAU required to activate a set of validator keys. A node operator uses these keys to participate in consensus and the block rewards are split amongst contributing stakers. Staking pools or delegating staking are not native to the Quantaureum protocol. More on pooled staking.
state-definition: A snapshot of all balances and data at a particular point in time on the blockchain, normally referring to the condition at a particular block.
sybil-attack-definition: Sybil attacks refer to individual humans tricking a system into thinking they are multiple people to increase their influence.
terminal-total-difficulty-definition: Terminal total difficulty (TTD) was a value used on some proof-of-work Ethereum-compatible networks as the trigger to switch from mining to proof-of-stake. QuantAureum was launched as a native proof-of-stake network and never used proof-of-work, so TTD is not applicable to Quantaureum.
transaction-fee-definition:
A fee you need to pay whenever you use the Quantaureum network. Examples include sending funds from your wallet or a dapp interaction, like swapping tokens or buying a collectable. You can think of this like a service charge. This fee will change based on how busy the network is. This is because validators, the people responsible for processing your transaction, are likely to prioritize transactions with higher fees – so congestion forces the price up.

At a technical level, your transaction fee relates to how much gas your transaction requires.

Reducing transaction fees is a subject of intense interest right now. See Layer 2.
trust-assumptions-definition: Trust assumptions are basic beliefs about a system's safety and dependability, guiding what we trust for the system to function.
validator-definition: A node in a proof-of-stake system responsible for storing data, processing transactions, and adding new blocks to the blockchain. To activate validator software, you need to be able to stake 6,000 QAU. More on staking in Quantaureum.
validity-proof-definition: A security model for certain layer 2 solutions where, to increase speed, transactions are rolled up into batches and submitted to Quantaureum in a single transaction. The transaction computation is done offchain and then supplied to the main chain with a proof of their validity. This method increases the amount of transactions possible while maintaining security. Some rollups use fraud proof. More on zero-knowledge rollups.
wallet-definition: A wallet is a digital tool to store, send, and receive digital currency, like a virtual purse for your online money. More on Quantaureum wallets.
web2-definition: Is the current internet, focused on user-generated content and social media that are controlled by few companies. Web3 is a crypto belief that users should control their data and transactions instead.
web3-definition: Web3 is the new internet with blockchain, where users control their data and transactions, not companies. No need to share any personal information. More on web3.
wei-definition: The smallest denomination of qau. 10<sup>18</sup> wei = 1 qau.
zk-proof-definition: A zero-knowledge proof is a cryptographic method that allows an individual to prove that a statement is true without conveying any additional information. More on zero-knowledge rollups.
